subject: US interest rates raised for first time in three years
posts:
The Fed just hiked US interest rates to 4% amid soaring energy costs and persistent inflation, sparking political friction.
Evidence: Rate hike to 4%, Oil price shocks, Political pushback
#Aletheia #Economy #US

The Federal Reserve raised interest rates in a unanimous vote to curb sticky inflation, weathering sharp political attacks.
Stated Judgement: (+0.5, 0.0) — Conditional Good

Higher borrowing costs squeeze consumers and credit card debt while geopolitical oil shocks drive broader price pressures.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.6, -0.7) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
The rate hike addresses inflation symptoms while shifting systemic debt burdens onto vulnerable borrowers.

Integrity: Meaningful Distortion (Hypocrisy: 5.2, z: 3)

- Federal Reserve: FAIL (-0.5, -0.6) — Uses monetary levers that penalize working borrowers.
- Political Opposition: FAIL (-0.7, -0.8) — Blames institutional actors for structural inflation.
The Federal Reserve lifted benchmark rates to a target range of 3.75% to 4%, marking the first hike in over three years as core inflation lingers well above target.

The Bright Side:
Higher yields offer much-needed relief and better returns for everyday savers after years of negative real rates.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing monetary policy tools (WHAT) with systemic economic health (WHO) masks the true burden borne by debtors.

Social Physics Analysis:
Central bankers run a smart selfish maneuver, using technical pretexts of price stability to cool demand while shielding asset holders from debt deflation.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map stated anti-inflation goals against crushing borrowing costs, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Systemic strain concentrates debt pressure downward.

The Unavoidable Truth: Higher interest rates increase debt servicing costs for ordinary households.

The Unavoidable Lie: Central bank rate hikes single-handedly solve supply-side commodity inflation.

Classic central bank move—raising rates to cool things down while everyone else gets squeezed on their car loans and credit cards.
